overview: Service protocol and monitoring plan for a nurse-led heart failure titration clinic, registered as a service evaluation; one main measure, one secondary measure and three balancing measures reviewed monthly.
population: Adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction under the hospital service who are below target doses of any indicated class, referred by a cardiologist or at discharge; patients under palliative care or with eGFR below 20 are excluded from titration.
exposure: Fortnightly clinic or telephone visits by a nurse prescriber, alternating where the patient wishes, with potassium and kidney function checked before each change at the clinic or a community site; dose changes follow the signed-off protocol for four classes with hold and referral rules.
procedures: Referral by cardiologist or at discharge; first visit within 2 weeks; one dose change per visit; potassium above 5.5 mmol/L holds the antagonist; systolic blood pressure below 95 mmHg with symptoms holds the next increase; eGFR fall above 30 percent triggers review with the cardiologist. Monthly measures are drawn from the clinic list and the laboratory system by the lead nurse and reviewed with the clinical lead.

outcomes.name: Patients at half target dose or more of all indicated classes
outcomes.measure: Proportion of patients 6 months after referral on at least half the target dose of every indicated class
outcomes.why: The measure the clinic exists to change; comparable with the June baseline.

outcomes.name: Heart failure hospitalisation
outcomes.measure: Admissions with heart failure as primary diagnosis within 12 months of referral, described without comparison

outcomes.name: Hyperkalaemia
outcomes.why: Main safety risk of four-class titration.

outcomes.name: Symptomatic hypotension or kidney function fall
outcomes.measure: Dose reduction for symptomatic hypotension or eGFR fall above 30 percent
outcomes.why: Harms that would outweigh faster titration.

outcomes.name: Missed titration visits by deprivation fifth
outcomes.measure: Missed scheduled visits divided by scheduled visits, by postcode deprivation fifth
outcomes.why: Checks that the clinic does not widen access gaps.

feasibility: Fits 6 nurse hours per week for about 12 active patients at a time; about 120 patients in the first year; data come from the clinic list and laboratory results already held.
biasMitigation: Measure definitions fixed before the clinic opens
Baseline from the six months before opening, using the same definition
Every referred patient counted, including those who stop attending

biasFlags.label: Referral selection
biasFlags.note: Cardiologists may refer patients most likely to tolerate titration; report referral numbers against the clinic list.

biasFlags.label: Tests outside the hospital
biasFlags.note: Primary care results may be missed; ask at each visit.

flags: Descriptive monitoring only; no adjusted models
parsimony.simplestPath: One main measure against a baseline, three balancing measures and one access measure, reviewed monthly.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the service protocol; the competence framework informs supervision of the first 20 patients.
summary: Service protocol with one main measure, one secondary, two balancing and one access measure.
